title: Quasi-projective morphisms compose over a quasi-compact base
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], both of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and suppose $S$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Suppose there exist an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $L$ and an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $M$ [def-sc-invertible-module] that are respectively $f$-relatively ample and $g$-relatively ample. Then $g\circ f$ is of finite type and there exists an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $N$ that is $(g\circ f)$-relatively ample. Here an invertible module $L$ on the source of a morphism $h$ is $h$-relatively ample if $h$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and, for every affine open $V$ of its target, $L|_{h^{-1}(V)}$ is ample in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Tag 0C4M (lemma-composition-quasi-projective), with Definition Tag 01VW(1) (definition-quasi-projective) and Definition Tag 01VH (definition-relatively-ample).

proof.text: Put $h=g\circ f$. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1), $h$ is of finite type. In particular $h$ is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This proves the finite-type clause and supplies the quasi-compactness needed by the affine-cover criterion below.

Choose an affine open cover of $S$ and a finite subcover $S=\bigcup_{i=1}^r V_i$, using [def-pc-scheme] and quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Set $Y_i=g^{-1}(V_i)$, $X_i=h^{-1}(V_i)$, and let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be the restriction of $f$. Put $L_i=L|_{X_i}$ and $M_i=M|_{Y_i}$. The morphism $f_i$ is the base change of $f$ by $Y_i\hookrightarrow Y$, hence is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](2), and is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Every affine open $W$ of $Y_i$ is an affine open of $Y$, and $f_i^{-1}(W)=f^{-1}(W)$. Thus $L_i$ is $f_i$-relatively ample directly from the hypothesis on $L$. The hypothesis on $M$, applied to the affine open $V_i$, says that $M_i$ is ample. Restrictions of the two invertible modules remain locally free of rank one by restricting their local trivializations [def-sc-invertible-module].

source.place: Tag 0C4K (lemma-ample-composition), finite affine covering and restriction; Tag 01VH (definition-relatively-ample); Tag 01T4 (lemma-base-change-finite-type).

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-relative-ample-absolute-twist] to $f_i,L_i,M_i$ for each $i$. All its hypotheses were checked in Step 2: quasi-compactness of $f_i$, relative ampleness of $L_i$, and absolute ampleness of $M_i$. Obtain $a_i\geq0$ such that $L_i\otimes f_i^*(M_i^{\otimes a})$ is ample on $X_i$ for every $a\geq a_i$. Choose $a=\max(\{0\}\cup\{a_i:1\leq i\leq r\})$. Then the same exponent works for every member of the finite cover. This also defines $a=0$ when the cover is empty; no bound over an infinite family is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0C4K (lemma-ample-composition), applying Tag 0892 (lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample)(1) on each cover member and taking a common sufficiently large exponent.

proof.text: Define $N=L\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}f^*(M^{\otimes a})$, using [def-pc-module-pullback] and [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The tensor power $M^{\otimes a}$ is invertible by [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]; its pullback and its tensor product with $L$ are invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1). If $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ and $k_i:Y_i\hookrightarrow Y$ are the inclusions, then $f\circ j_i=k_i\circ f_i$. Parts (2) of that same node, applied to these maps and iterated over the $a$ factors, give $j_i^*N\cong L_i\otimes f_i^*(M_i^{\otimes a})$. For $a=0$, the comparison of units is the defining map $\mathcal O_{X_i}\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y_i}}\mathcal O_{Y_i}\cong\mathcal O_{X_i}$, $b\otimes c\mapsto b f_i^{\sharp}(c)$, with inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. Pullback by an open inclusion is restriction, since $j_i^{-1}\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X_i}$ in the pullback formula of [def-pc-module-pullback]. Consequently $N|_{X_i}$ is ample by Step 3; isomorphisms preserve the affine nonvanishing loci in the definition of ampleness [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Tag 0C4K (lemma-ample-composition), the displayed twist and its restrictions; Modules Tags 01CD (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), 0B8L (lemma-pullback-invertible), 01CT (lemma-constructions-invertible), and Sheaves Tag 0097 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-affine-cover] to $h:X\to S$, the invertible module $N$, and the affine open covering $(V_i)$. Step 1 supplies quasi-compactness of $h$, and Step 4 supplies ampleness of $N|_{h^{-1}(V_i)}$. The cited statement gives ampleness of $N|_{h^{-1}(V)}$ for every affine open $V\subseteq S$. Together with quasi-compactness of $h$, this is precisely $h$-relative ampleness as defined in the item. The already established finite-type clause finishes the conclusion, including the empty-base case, where any morphism to the empty scheme has empty source.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q47-00d1475ee (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, its 5 steps and every cited statement. There are no new nodes, and the statement is unchanged apart from TeX escapes (finite-type f and g, quasi-compact S, L f-ample, M g-ample). The steps follow Stacks morphisms.tex 0C4M = 01T3 + 0C4K exactly. Step 1: g∘f is of finite type by the sfb node (1), 01T3. Step 2: finite affine cover V_i of S; f_i : f^{-1}(Y_i) → Y_i has finite type by sfb (2); L_i is f_i-ample because affine opens of Y_i are affine opens of Y with the same preimage; M_i is ample by g-ampleness at V_i. Step 3: the twist node (0892(1)) gives every a ≥ a_i, so a = max({0} ∪ {a_i}) works on every V_i. Step 4: N = L⊗f^*M^{⊗a} is invertible and restricts to L_i⊗f_i^*M_i^{⊗a}, by the tensor-pullback node (1)/(2) applied to f∘j_i = k_i∘f_i; open pullback is restriction; the a=0 case is written out. Step 5: the 01VJ (3)⇒(1) affine-cover node gives h-ampleness. The empty base and the affine base (which reduces to 0892(1)) were checked. Duplicate search over 0C4K, 0C4M, 0892 and 'relatively ample' found only the Noetherian-affine special case (not cited, no cycle) and the 0892(2)/0893/01VU nodes, which state different results. The two declared tool_uses are generic and accepted. Batch-5 flag on lem-trf-scheme-relative-ample-affine-cover: it is Stacks 01VJ, general scheme theory that neither assumption gives. Its full closure (1205 nodes) has only generic sec-trace-formula nodes: algebraic spaces, Proj/twist, the 01VJ canonical-Proj criterion, the Zariski–étale quasi-coherent equivalence and 036W descent. It contains no thm-trf, no trace-transport node, no Poincaré node and no batch-4 target, so it is accepted, not RETURNed. No changes.
